structured_output.summary: The outermost RequestBodyLimitMiddleware now defers the Content-Length fail-fast until the limit is final. Nested instances update the tracked limit and keep their immediate check. I couldn't run tests here, so none of this has been run.

criteria_notes.note: test_nested_limits_raise_and_lower_the_outer_limit: outer 10 and inner 100 with a 50-byte body and Content-Length: 50 returns 200, and the endpoint saw limit 100.

test_content_length_failfast, test_content_length_failfast_sends_exactly_one_response and test_content_length_failfast_when_app_returns_without_response cover this. The endpoint never reads the body and the client gets plain-text 413 "Content Too Large". Exactly one start and one body message are sent. The case where the app returns without a response is covered too. I changed test_content_length_failfast, which used to assert the endpoint was not called. It now asserts the endpoint is called and its response is replaced.
test_understated_content_length_and_exact_limit (understated header, exact limit, unparsable header) and test_limit_enforced_without_content_length (no header).
test_no_double_response: after the response has started, HTTPException(413) is re-raised and only http.response.start was sent. The existing test, unchanged.
test_scope_key: the key holds the limit while the app runs, and its previous value or absence is restored afterwards. The existing test, unchanged.
